amendments.reason: Production Chrome serializes inline fractional CSS positions to three decimal places; an exact floating-point equality check rejected correct output by under 0.001 CSS pixels during the excluded smoke run.
amendments.change: Final x/y output parity is accepted within 0.01 CSS pixels. No latency threshold, page count, arm, or workload changed.

question: Do retained-VDOM per-frame paths keep their measured update advantage after including mount and teardown JavaScript cost for one fixed-topology animated scene?

relationship.followUpReason: V6 measured mount and update cost, but excluded teardown, page load, and compilation from its post-hoc mount-amortization estimate.
relationship.scope: This study adds teardown and an observed 300-frame lifecycle workload. It does not estimate network/parse/compile cost or dynamic topology.

arms.react: React 19.3 + build-verified React Compiler; ReactBoard with per-segment useSyncExternalStore snapshots over the same x/y columns.
arms.runtime-vdom: Retained VDOM with a shared frame source, reading the precomputed Float64Array x/y columns through mount-resolved bindings.
arms.columnar-vdom: Retained VDOM with OXC-generated binding IDs resolved to contiguous Float64Array x/y columns at mount; one column batch per frame.

design.replicationUnit: One fresh visible production browser page; five paired page blocks per size.
lifecycle: allocate model, sources/store, bindings, and host tree
run and record 300 measured RAF updates
verify final output and stable host identity
dispose/unmount, clear harness references, and assert empty host container and zero subscriber registrations
design.primaryMetric: measured JavaScript cycle cost = mountMs + sum(updateCpuMs for the 300 measured frames) + teardownMs; RAF wait time is excluded.
secondaryMetrics: full RAF elapsed time including warmup and display waits
heap usage before mount, after mount, after updates, and after teardown when browser memory API is available
design.pairing: Within each replication block, compare React and each VDOM arm at matching segment counts. Pages are randomized from the saved schedule; frames are nested samples.
exclusions: navigation, network, JavaScript parse/evaluation, and OXC compilation cost from the primary cycle metric
layout, paint, GPU work, and physical presentation
dynamic segment growth/removal during the measured run

correctness: final segment and food positions match the deterministic model within 0.01 CSS pixels
host count and node identities remain stable during the update window
React external-store listener registrations are zero after root unmount
VDOM binding registrations and retained host nodes are zero after dispose
all three arms have an empty host container after teardown
page is visible and uses the verified production build

hypotheses.lifecycleAdvantage: Columnar VDOM primary cycle cost is <=0.90x React on at least four of five paired page blocks at both 512 and 1,024 segments.
hypotheses.updateCostPreserved: Columnar VDOM updateCpuMs median is no greater than React on at least four of five pages at both sizes.
hypotheses.correctness: Every accepted page passes all lifecycle and output contracts.

decisionRules.pass: All correctness pages pass, lifecycleAdvantage passes at both sizes, and updateCostPreserved passes at both sizes.
decisionRules.fail: Any correctness failure or any missed latency threshold is reported; do not exclude pages or revise thresholds after collection.
decisionRules.interpretation: A pass establishes only a same-device, fixed-topology JavaScript-cycle-cost advantage for these arms and sizes. It does not establish a full cold-start win, smoothness, dynamic-topology performance, or a general React speedup.

environment.targetBrowser: Chrome production build; record exact UA, browser version, platform, hardware concurrency, DPR, viewport, and visibility on every page.
environment.device: Reuse the V6 device/profile for this lifecycle follow-up; an independent physical device remains a separate confirmatory gate.
environment.sourceLock: Freeze the dedicated harness, Vite config, OXC-generated plan, package/Deno lockfiles, and built assets before collecting the first page.
